_note: Every lead is fictional: real ZIP codes with invented street names, phones in the 555-0100 to 555-0199 range reserved for fiction, emails on .example domains. Each scenario carries 'now', the instant the test clock reads when the lead reaches n8n (a few seconds after the customer submitted it), so the scenarios are spread over one October 2026 week in each branch's own time zone. Payload shapes: web_form is a Gravity Forms webhook entry, hubspot_form a HubSpot form submission, call_tracking a CallRail-style post-call webhook with a transcript.

scenarios.description: Slack answers the leads summary with HTTP 429 and Retry-After: 1 once (its chat.postMessage limit is about one message per second per channel). n8n's fixed 5-second retry waits longer than Slack asked, the second try posts, and exactly one message exists.

HubSpot commits the deal but its answer arrives after the node timeout, and (like HubSpot) ignores Idempotency-Key, so n8n's retries conflict on the unique ridgeway_event_id. The workflow reads the deal by ridgeway_event_id and goes on with it: one deal.

A contact with the lead's email exists, but HubSpot's search has not indexed it yet, so the search finds nothing and the create is refused with 409 (the email exists). The workflow reads the contact by email (idProperty=email) and updates it: no second contact.

redelivery_while_in_flight.description: A second POST of the same event arrives while the first is still running (the mock answers Claude 5 seconds late): 409 with Retry-After and status in_flight. After the first finishes, a third POST gets duplicate. One deal, one task.

redelivery_after_failure.description: The first run fails at the ClickUp CSR task (503 on all four tries) after the deal exists; the error workflow gives the claim back; the redelivery succeeds. The mock ignores Idempotency-Key on deal creation, like HubSpot, so only the search by ridgeway_event_id can prevent a second deal. Exactly one deal, one task.
